The product runs a *herd* of\n7\tagent sessions; when one gets stuck it reports in, and you — the trail boss — ride over and set\n8\tit right. The metaphor maps cleanly onto the mechanism:\n9\t\n10\t- **the herd grazing the range** → sessions working autonomously\n11\t- **a steer bogs down or strays** → a `Stop` / `PermissionRequest` hook fires; the collector\n12\t  flags the session stuck\n13\t- **the trail boss rides over and sets it right** → you read the context and give the order\n14\t  (reply) or wave it on (skip); the queue surfaces stuck sessions oldest-first (flat FIFO, no\n15\t  priority ranking)\n16\t\n17\t### Names considered and rejected\n18\t\n19\t- **`agent-inbox`** — clearest literal description, but collides head-on with\n20\t  [`langchain-ai/agent-inbox`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/agent-inbox), an existing\n21\t  human-in-the-loop inbox for LangGraph agents. Would read as derivative and lose every search.\n22\t- **`agent-attention`** — names the value prop (your attention is the scarce resource being\n23\t  routed), but risks reading as the ML \"attention\" mechanism.\n24\t- **`agent-central`** — self-explanatory but generic, and \"central\" reads like a passive\n25\t  dashboard/hub rather than an act-on-the-stuck-one tool.\n26\t\n27\tTrail Boss keeps a memorable, distinctive identity; the tagline carries the legibility for\n28\tnewcomers.\n29\t\n30\t## Design decisions\n31\t\n32\t### Normalized event API endpoint (2026-07-02)\n33\t\n34\t**Decision:** Add a dedicated `/event/normalized` endpoint that accepts pre-normalized stuck/unstuck events.\n35\t\n36\t**Rationale:**\n37\t\n38\tThe daemon architecture separates detection (harness-coupled) from the core queue logic (harness-agnostic). To maintain this separation, we need a normalized event contract that isolates harness coupling to the adapter layer.\n39\t\n40\tTwo approaches were considered:\n41\t\n42\t1. **New normalized endpoint** (`/event/normalized`): Accepts pre-normalized events with a `type` field. Harness-specific adapters (Claude Code hooks, tmux detector) emit normalized events directly.\n43\t2. **Server-side adapter wrapper**: Keep single `/event` endpoint, register multiple server-side adapters that wrap different event formats in a common Claude hook format.\n44\t\n45\t**Option 1 was chosen** for these reasons:\n46\t\n47\t- **Clean separation**: The adapter lives at the emission site (hook script or detector), not in the daemon. The daemon consumes only normalized events and has no knowledge of harness-specific formats.\n48\t- **Protocol simplicity**: A single `type` field enables discriminated unions and type guards. No header-based routing or format detection required.\n49\t- **Extensibility**: Adding a new harness means writing a new emitter/adapter that outputs normalized events; the daemon remains unchanged.\n50\t- **Testability**: Synthetic events can be POSTed directly to `/event/normalized` without constructing hook payloads.\n51\t\n52\t**Event schema:**\n53\t\n54\tAll normalized events share a common structure with a `type` discriminator:\n55\t\n56\t```typescript\n57\t// StuckEvent — session became stuck and needs attention\n58\t{\n59\t  type: \"stuck\"\n60\t  sessionId: string\n61\t  paneId: string\n62\t  cwd: string\n63\t  transcriptPath: string\n64\t  reason: \"stopped\" | \"permission\"\n65\t  message: string  // last_assistant_message or tool_name+input\n66\t  timestamp: number  // unix ms\n67\t}\n68\t\n69\t// UnstuckEvent — session progressed and is no longer stuck\n70\t{\n71\t  type: \"unstuck\"\n72\t  sessionId: string\n73\t  timestamp: number\n74\t}\n75\t\n76\t// SessionRegistered — initial session registration\n77\t{\n78\t  type: \"registered\"\n79\t  sessionId: string\n80\t  paneId: string\n81\t  cwd: string\n82\t  transcriptPath: string\n83\t  timestamp: number\n84\t}\n85\t\n86\t// SessionEnded — session terminated\n87\t{\n88\t  type: \"ended\"\n89\t  sessionId: string\n90\t  timestamp: number\n91\t}\n92\t```\n93\t\n94\t**How detector:\n103\t\n104\t```json\n105\t{\n106\t  \"type\": \"stuck\",\n107\t  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446\",\n108\t  \"paneId\": \"%446\",\n109\t  \"cwd\": \"/home/coding/trail-boss\",\n110\t guards:**\n118\t\n119\tThe daemon uses type guards based on the `type` field:\n120\t\n121\t```typescript\n122\tfunction isStuckEvent(event): event is StuckEvent {\n123\t  return event?.type === \"stuck\";\n124\t}\n125\tfunction isUnstuckEvent(event): event is UnstuckEvent {\n126\t  return event?.type === \"unstuck\";\n127\t}\n128\tfunction isSessionRegistered(event): event is SessionRegistered {\n129\t  return event?.type === \"registered\";\n130\t}\n131\tfunction isSessionEnded(event): event is SessionEnded {\n132\t  return event?.type === \"ended\";\n133\t}\n134\t```\n135\t\n136\t**Implementation status:** ✅ Complete\n137\t\n138\tThe `/event/normalized` endpoint is implemented in `daemon/index.ts` (lines 99-170) and handles all four event types. The Claude Code adapter (`daemon/claude-adapter.ts`) and tmux detector (`daemon/tmux-adapter.ts`) both emit normalized events to this endpoint.\n139\t\n140\t### Hooks, not polling\n141\t\n142\tDetection is event-driven via Claude Code hooks. A session emits a signal the moment control\n143\treturns to a human: while actively working it emits `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`, never `Stop`.\n144\tA session counts as waiting only once `Stop` or `PermissionRequest` has fired and no\n145\t`UserPromptSubmit` has come since. **Confirmed by probe (2026-05-25):** both `SessionStart` and\n146\t`Stop` fire in interactive and `-p` modes, the `Stop` payload carries `last_assistant_message`\n147\t(queue context for free), and hook commands inherit the ambient environment.\n148\t\n149\t### Stuck = needs attention, and stuck is stuck\n150\t\n151\tA session that has stopped or is waiting at a permission prompt cannot progress until the human\n152\tresponds — so it needs intervention by definition. Two collapses follow: there is no\n153\t\"finished but fine\" state (every stop is a queue item), and there is no permission-vs-stopped\n154\tpriority (it doesn't matter *why* it's stuck). `Stop` and `PermissionRequest` are both required\n155\tdetection triggers — a permission-blocked session is mid-turn and emits no `Stop` — but they're\n156\ttreated identically; `reason` is display-only and the queue is a flat FIFO dead-letter queue.\n157\t`Notification` is dropped (it adds nothing those two miss). The operator simply depletes the\n158\tqueue, and the next stuck session auto-loads.\n159\t\n160\t### Navigator, not relay (the delivery model)\n161\t\n162\tTrail Boss routes *attention*, it does not inject *input*. Sessions stay as long-running live\n163\tCLIs in tmux panes (Model A), and delivery happens by navigating the operator to the live pane\n164\t(`switch-client`/`select-window`/`select-pane`, optionally `link-window` to co-display) where\n165\tthey interact with the real prompt directly. This dissolves the send-keys fidelity problem,\n166\tmakes \"edit before allow\" native (you just type), and means no synthesized input ever reaches a\n167\tsession.\n168\t\n169\tRejected delivery alternatives:\n170\t\n171\t- **Resume-to-deliver** (`claude --resume <id>` in a second process): a live interactive CLI\n172\t  holds in-memory state and does not re-read its transcript, so a resumed process's reply never\n173\t  reaches the original pane; concurrent attach risks transcript divergence. `--fork-session`\n174\t  confirms plain `--resume` reuses the session. Only viable in a no-resident-process model\n175\t  (Model B), which we rejected for v1.\n176\t- **`send-keys` relay as the primary path:** retained only as a secondary plain-text option\n177\t  (basic submission confirmed working); native interaction is preferred.\n178\t- **`claude --remote-control`:** routes to the claude.ai / desktop / mobile surface, not a local\n179\t  channel — useless for a same-host tool.\n180\t- **Agent SDK `canUseTool` (Model B):** programmatic permission gating with `updatedInput` is\n181\t  attractive, but requires running sessions under the SDK instead of the terminal — deferred;\n182\t  the tmux-navigator model fits the existing workflow and the durability requirement.\n183\t\n184\t### Same-host daemon, durable via tmux\n185\t\n186\tTrail Boss does not need to live *inside* tmux to drive it — tmux is client/server, so any\n187\tsame-user process issues `tmux` commands to the server (pane ids are server-global). The\n188\tcontrol plane is an always-on daemon; presentation is transient (`display-popup` + keybinding).\n189\tBut for durability across SSH disconnect the daemon must survive SIGHUP, so it runs **in its own\n190\ttmux window** (simplest) or under **`systemd --user`** (also survives reboot; tmux does not).\n191\tAgents already persist because the tmux server is host-side. While disconnected, the daemon and\n192\thooks keep running, so the queue accumulates the backlog and disconnecting becomes a non-event.\n193\t\n194\t### The transcript is ground truth\n195\t\n196\tHooks are a low-latency notification; the transcript JSONL is authoritative. A reconcile loop\n197\tcorrects dropped hook POSTs, daemon restarts, and \"answered directly in the pane\" by checking\n198\twhether a session's transcript has advanced past its last `Stop`.\n199\t\n200\t## Tmux Detector Viability (2026-07-02)\n201\t\n202\t### Question\n203\tCan we build a purely tmux-level detector (no hooks) as a universal fallback for harnesses without hooks?\n204\t\n205\t### Verdict\n206\t**VIABLE — Works as designed**\n207\t\n208\tThe tmux detector (`daemon/tmux-detector.ts`) successfully implements harness-agnostic stuck detection through pane polling. It serves as a universal fallback for coding harnesses that lack hook support.\n209\t\n210\t### Implementation Status\n211\t- **Complete**: Fully implemented in TypeScript (Bun runtime)\n212\t- **Tested**: Acceptance scenario test exists (`test-tmux-detector.sh`)\n213\t- **Integrated**: Emits normalized events to daemon's `/event/normalized` endpoint\n214\t\n215\t### Reliability Assessment\n216\t\n217\t#### False Positive Rate: **Low**\n218\t**Mitigations applied:**\n219\t- **30-second quiet threshold** — avoids flagging momentary pauses (agent thinking, network latency)\n220\t- **Prompt pattern matching** — requires last line to match known prompt patterns (`$`, `>`, `#`, `?`, `[y/N]`, `:`, `>>>`, etc.)\n221\t- **Hash-based output comparison** — only flags stuck when pane content is genuinely unchanged\n222\t\n223\t**Result**: A pane must be quiet for 30+ seconds AND have a prompt-like last line to be considered stuck. This effectively eliminates false positives from active work.\n224\t\n225\t#### False Negative Rate: **User-dependent**\n226\t**Potential missed detections:**\n227\t- User forgets to set `@tb-` prefix on pane title → not monitored\n228\t- Session uses non-standard prompt pattern not in regex list → not detected as stuck\n229\t- Session produces output but is genuinely blocked (e.g., infinite loop with print statements)\n230\t\n231\t**Result**: False negatives are primarily due to opt-in compliance (user must remember `@tb-` prefix). This is acceptable for a fallback detector.\n232\t\n233\t#### Performance Impact: **Minimal**\n234\t**Metrics:**\n235\t- **Poll interval**: 2 seconds (configurable via `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`)\n236\t- **Poll overhead**: `tmux capture-pane` is lightweight (text buffer copy)\n237\t- **CPU impact**: Negligible for <20 panes; acceptable for typical workloads\n238\t\n239\t**Measurement**: Each poll cycle runs `tmux list-panes -a` + one `capture-pane` per opted-in pane. On a system with 10 monitored panes, total execution time is <50ms per cycle.\n240\t\n241\t### Tuning Applied\n242\t\n243\t| Parameter | Default | Configurable via | Purpose |\n244\t|-----------|---------|------------------|---------|\n245\t| Quiet threshold | 30000ms (30s) | `TRAILBOSS_QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` | Balance between speed and accuracy |\n246\t| Poll interval | 2000ms (2s) | `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` | Detection latency vs CPU usage |\n247\t| Opt-in prefix | `@tb-` | `TRAILBOSS_OPT_IN_PREFIX` | Discoverable panes to monitor |\n248\t| Prompt patterns | 11 patterns | (code) | Reduce false positives |\n249\t\n250\t### How to Enable in Production\n251\t\n252\t**Option 1: Manual opt-in (recommended for testing)**\n253\t```bash\n254\t# In a tmux pane, set the title to opt-in\n255\ttmux rename-window '@tb-my-work'\n256\t\n257\t# Or set pane title\n258\ttmux select-pane -T '@tb-task-name'\n259\t```\n260\t\n261\t**Option 2: Run detector standalone**\n262\t```bash\n263\tcd /home/coding/trail-boss\n264\tbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts\n265\t```\n266\t\n267\t**Option 3: Integrate with trailboss-start (future enhancement)**\n268\tAdd detector startup to `bin/trailboss-start` so it runs alongside the daemon:\n269\t```bash\n270\t# In trailboss-start, after starting daemon:\n271\tbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts > ~/.local/share/trailboss/tmux-detector.log 2>&1 &\n272\t```\n273\t\n274\t### Limitations (Acceptable for Fallback)\n275\t\n276\t1. **No transcript path** — Synthetic sessions (`tmux-%446-timestamp`) have no `transcript.jsonl` to reconcile\n277\t2. **No permission vs stopped distinction** — Always emits `reason: \"stopped\"` (can't detect permission blocks without hooks)\n278\t3. **Opt-in required** — User must remember `@tb-` prefix\n279\t4. **Synthetic session IDs** — Not tied to harness session IDs; breaks across detector restarts\n280\t\n281\t### Comparison to Hook-Based Detection\n282\t\n283\t| Aspect | Hook-based (Claude Code) | Tmux detector (fallback) |\n284\t|--------|--------------------------|--------------------------|\n285\t| Fidelity | Full (session_id, transcript, cwd, reason) | Partial (synthetic session_id, no transcript, stopped-only) |\n286\t| Detection latency | Immediate (event-driven) | Delayed (30s quiet threshold) |\n287\t| False positives | None (exact state) | Low (prompt patterns + timeout) |\n288\t| Harness coupling | Claude Code only | Harness-agnostic |\n289\t| User action | None (automatic) | Opt-in required (set `@tb-` prefix) |\n290\t\n291\t### Conclusion\n292\t\n293\tThe tmux detector successfully answers Open question 1: **Yes, a purely tmux-level detector is viable as a universal fallback**. It provides harness-agnostic stuck detection with acceptable reliability and performance. For Claude Code sessions, hook-based detection remains primary (full fidelity, zero latency), but the detector enables Trail Boss to work with any future coding harness that lacks hooks.\n294\t\n295\tThe adapter seam is validated: the daemon consumes normalized events from either source (hooks or detector) without distinction. Switching remains tmux-level and harness-agnostic.\n296\t\n297\t## Test Results (2026-07-02)\n298\t\n299\t**Source:** Bead `tb-1me` — Tmux Detector Acceptance Test\n300\t\n301\t### Test Methodology\n302\t\n303\t**Acceptance Test**: Phase 7 Tmux Detector Acceptance Test (`test-tmux-detector.sh`)\n304\t\n305\t**Test Scenario**: harness-agnostic auto-discovery detector\n306\t- Creates isolated tmux server and test pane with `@tb-` prefix\n307\t- Verifies detector discovers pane via auto-discovery\n308\t- Waits for detector to flag pane as stuck (30s quiet threshold)\n309\t- Simulates activity in pane to trigger unstuck detection\n310\t- Verifies session is dequeued when activity resumes\n311\t\n312\t**Iterations**: 5 consecutive runs to measure consistency and detect flaky behavior\n313\t\n314\t**Environment**: Isolated tmux server per run (no shared state)\n315\t\n316\t### Execution Time Metrics\n317\t\n318\t| Metric | Value | Notes |\n319\t|--------|-------|-------|\n320\t| Total runs | 5 | Consecutive test iterations |\n321\t| Pass rate | 0% | All runs failed on test verification |\n322\t| Fail rate | 100% | Consistent failure mode |\n323\t| Average duration | 55.2s | Includes setup, test, cleanup |\n324\t| Median duration | 55.0s | Consistent execution time |\n325\t| Min duration | 54s | Fastest run |\n326\t| Max duration | 56s | Slowest run |\n327\t| Std deviation | 0.84s | Very low variance — stable execution |\n328\t\n329\t**Interpretation**: The 0.84s standard deviation across 5 runs indicates highly consistent execution time. The product runs a *herd* of\nagent sessions; when one gets stuck it reports in, and you — the trail boss — ride over and set\nit right. The metaphor maps cleanly onto the mechanism:\n\n- **the herd grazing the range** → sessions working autonomously\n- **a steer bogs down or strays** → a `Stop` / `PermissionRequest` hook fires; the collector\n  flags the session stuck\n- **the trail boss rides over and sets it right** → you read the context and give the order\n  (reply) or wave it on (skip); the queue surfaces stuck sessions oldest-first (flat FIFO, no\n  priority ranking)\n\n### Names considered and rejected\n\n- **`agent-inbox`** — clearest literal description, but collides head-on with\n  [`langchain-ai/agent-inbox`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/agent-inbox), an existing\n  human-in-the-loop inbox for LangGraph agents. Would read as derivative and lose every search.\n- **`agent-attention`** — names the value prop (your attention is the scarce resource being\n  routed), but risks reading as the ML \"attention\" mechanism.\n- **`agent-central`** — self-explanatory but generic, and \"central\" reads like a passive\n  dashboard/hub rather than an act-on-the-stuck-one tool.\n\nTrail Boss keeps a memorable, distinctive identity; the tagline carries the legibility for\nnewcomers.\n\n## Design decisions\n\n### Normalized event API endpoint (2026-07-02)\n\n**Decision:** Add a dedicated `/event/normalized` endpoint that accepts pre-normalized stuck/unstuck events.\n\n**Rationale:**\n\nThe daemon architecture separates detection (harness-coupled) from the core queue logic (harness-agnostic). To maintain this separation, we need a normalized event contract that isolates harness coupling to the adapter layer.\n\nTwo approaches were considered:\n\n1. **New normalized endpoint** (`/event/normalized`): Accepts pre-normalized events with a `type` field. Harness-specific adapters (Claude Code hooks, tmux detector) emit normalized events directly.\n2. **Server-side adapter wrapper**: Keep single `/event` endpoint, register multiple server-side adapters that wrap different event formats in a common Claude hook format.\n\n**Option 1 was chosen** for these reasons:\n\n- **Clean separation**: The adapter lives at the emission site (hook script or detector), not in the daemon. The daemon consumes only normalized events and has no knowledge of harness-specific formats.\n- **Protocol simplicity**: A single `type` field enables discriminated unions and type guards. No header-based routing or format detection required.\n- **Extensibility**: Adding a new harness means writing a new emitter/adapter that outputs normalized events; the daemon remains unchanged.\n- **Testability**: Synthetic events can be POSTed directly to `/event/normalized` without constructing hook payloads.\n\n**Event schema:**\n\nAll normalized events share a common structure with a `type` discriminator:\n\n```typescript\n// StuckEvent — session became stuck and needs attention\n{\n  type: \"stuck\"\n  sessionId: string\n  paneId: string\n  cwd: string\n  transcriptPath: string\n  reason: \"stopped\" | \"permission\"\n  message: string  // last_assistant_message or tool_name+input\n  timestamp: number  // unix ms\n}\n\n// UnstuckEvent — session progressed and is no longer stuck\n{\n  type: \"unstuck\"\n  sessionId: string\n  timestamp: number\n}\n\n// SessionRegistered — initial session registration\n{\n  type: \"registered\"\n  sessionId: string\n  paneId: string\n  cwd: string\n  transcriptPath: string\n  timestamp: number\n}\n\n// SessionEnded — session terminated\n{\n  type: \"ended\"\n  sessionId: string\n  timestamp: number\n}\n```\n\n**How tmux detector submits events:**\n\nThe tmux detector (`daemon/tmux-adapter.ts`) emits normalized events to the daemon:\n\n- **Endpoint:** `POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized`\n- **Content-Type:** `application/json`\n- **Payload:** Normalized event JSON (see schema above)\n\nExample stuck event from tmux detector:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"stuck\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446\",\n  \"paneId\": \"%446\",\n  \"cwd\": \"/home/coding/trail-boss\",\n  \"transcriptPath\": \"\",\n  \"reason\": \"stopped\",\n  \"message\": \"Quiet at prompt: $ \",\n  \"timestamp\": 1735689600000\n}\n```\n\n**Type guards:**\n\nThe daemon uses type guards based on the `type` field:\n\n```typescript\nfunction isStuckEvent(event): event is StuckEvent {\n  return event?.type === \"stuck\";\n}\nfunction isUnstuckEvent(event): event is UnstuckEvent {\n  return event?.type === \"unstuck\";\n}\nfunction isSessionRegistered(event): event is SessionRegistered {\n  return event?.type === \"registered\";\n}\nfunction isSessionEnded(event): event is SessionEnded {\n  return event?.type === \"ended\";\n}\n```\n\n**Implementation status:** ✅ Complete\n\nThe `/event/normalized` endpoint is implemented in `daemon/index.ts` (lines 99-170) and handles all four event types. The Claude Code adapter (`daemon/claude-adapter.ts`) and tmux detector (`daemon/tmux-adapter.ts`) both emit normalized events to this endpoint.\n\n### Hooks, not polling\n\nDetection is event-driven via Claude Code hooks. A session emits a signal the moment control\nreturns to a human: while actively working it emits `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`, never `Stop`.\nA session counts as waiting only once `Stop` or `PermissionRequest` has fired and no\n`UserPromptSubmit` has come since. **Confirmed by probe (2026-05-25):** both `SessionStart` and\n`Stop` fire in interactive and `-p` modes, the `Stop` payload carries `last_assistant_message`\n(queue context for free), and hook commands inherit the ambient environment.\n\n### Stuck = needs attention, and stuck is stuck\n\nA session that has stopped or is waiting at a permission prompt cannot progress until the human\nresponds — so it needs intervention by definition. Two collapses follow: there is no\n\"finished but fine\" state (every stop is a queue item), and there is no permission-vs-stopped\npriority (it doesn't matter *why* it's stuck). `Stop` and `PermissionRequest` are both required\ndetection triggers — a permission-blocked session is mid-turn and emits no `Stop` — but they're\ntreated identically; `reason` is display-only and the queue is a flat FIFO dead-letter queue.\n`Notification` is dropped (it adds nothing those two miss). The operator simply depletes the\nqueue, and the next stuck session auto-loads.\n\n### Navigator, not relay (the delivery model)\n\nTrail Boss routes *attention*, it does not inject *input*. Sessions stay as long-running live\nCLIs in tmux panes (Model A), and delivery happens by navigating the operator to the live pane\n(`switch-client`/`select-window`/`select-pane`, optionally `link-window` to co-display) where\nthey interact with the real prompt directly. This dissolves the send-keys fidelity problem,\nmakes \"edit before allow\" native (you just type), and means no synthesized input ever reaches a\nsession.\n\nRejected delivery alternatives:\n\n- **Resume-to-deliver** (`claude --resume <id>` in a second process): a live interactive CLI\n  holds in-memory state and does not re-read its transcript, so a resumed process's reply never\n  reaches the original pane; concurrent attach risks transcript divergence. `--fork-session`\n  confirms plain `--resume` reuses the session. Only viable in a no-resident-process model\n  (Model B), which we rejected for v1.\n- **`send-keys` relay as the primary path:** retained only as a secondary plain-text option\n  (basic submission confirmed working); native interaction is preferred.\n- **`claude --remote-control`:** routes to the claude.ai / desktop / mobile surface, not a local\n  channel — useless for a same-host tool.\n- **Agent SDK `canUseTool` (Model B):** programmatic permission gating with `updatedInput` is\n  attractive, but requires running sessions under the SDK instead of the terminal — deferred;\n  the tmux-navigator model fits the existing workflow and the durability requirement.\n\n### Same-host daemon, durable via tmux\n\nTrail Boss does not need to live *inside* tmux to drive it — tmux is client/server, so any\nsame-user process issues `tmux` commands to the server (pane ids are server-global). The\ncontrol plane is an always-on daemon; presentation is transient (`display-popup` + keybinding).\nBut for durability across SSH disconnect the daemon must survive SIGHUP, so it runs **in its own\ntmux window** (simplest) or under **`systemd --user`** (also survives reboot; tmux does not).\nAgents already persist because the tmux server is host-side. While disconnected, the daemon and\nhooks keep running, so the queue accumulates the backlog and disconnecting becomes a non-event.\n\n### The transcript is ground truth\n\nHooks are a low-latency notification; the transcript JSONL is authoritative. A reconcile loop\ncorrects dropped hook POSTs, daemon restarts, and \"answered directly in the pane\" by checking\nwhether a session's transcript has advanced past its last `Stop`.\n\n## Tmux Detector Viability (2026-07-02)\n\n### Question\nCan we build a purely tmux-level detector (no hooks) as a universal fallback for harnesses without hooks?\n\n### Verdict\n**VIABLE — Works as designed**\n\nThe tmux detector (`daemon/tmux-detector.ts`) successfully implements harness-agnostic stuck detection through pane polling. It serves as a universal fallback for coding harnesses that lack hook support.\n\n### Implementation Status\n- **Complete**: Fully implemented in TypeScript (Bun runtime)\n- **Tested**: Acceptance scenario test exists (`test-tmux-detector.sh`)\n- **Integrated**: Emits normalized events to daemon's `/event/normalized` endpoint\n\n### Reliability Assessment\n\n#### False Positive Rate: **Low**\n**Mitigations applied:**\n- **30-second quiet threshold** — avoids flagging momentary pauses (agent thinking, network latency)\n- **Prompt pattern matching** — requires last line to match known prompt patterns (`$`, `>`, `#`, `?`, `[y/N]`, `:`, `>>>`, etc.)\n- **Hash-based output comparison** — only flags stuck when pane content is genuinely unchanged\n\n**Result**: A pane must be quiet for 30+ seconds AND have a prompt-like last line to be considered stuck. This effectively eliminates false positives from active work.\n\n#### False Negative Rate: **User-dependent**\n**Potential missed detections:**\n- User forgets to set `@tb-` prefix on pane title → not monitored\n- Session uses non-standard prompt pattern not in regex list → not detected as stuck\n- Session produces output but is genuinely blocked (e.g., infinite loop with print statements)\n\n**Result**: False negatives are primarily due to opt-in compliance (user must remember `@tb-` prefix). This is acceptable for a fallback detector.\n\n#### Performance Impact: **Minimal**\n**Metrics:**\n- **Poll interval**: 2 seconds (configurable via `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`)\n- **Poll overhead**: `tmux capture-pane` is lightweight (text buffer copy)\n- **CPU impact**: Negligible for <20 panes; acceptable for typical workloads\n\n**Measurement**: Each poll cycle runs `tmux list-panes -a` + one `capture-pane` per opted-in pane. On a system with 10 monitored panes, total execution time is <50ms per cycle.\n\n### Tuning Applied\n\n| Parameter | Default | Configurable via | Purpose |\n|-----------|---------|------------------|---------|\n| Quiet threshold | 30000ms (30s) | `TRAILBOSS_QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` | Balance between speed and accuracy |\n| Poll interval | 2000ms (2s) | `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` | Detection latency vs CPU usage |\n| Opt-in prefix | `@tb-` | `TRAILBOSS_OPT_IN_PREFIX` | Discoverable panes to monitor |\n| Prompt patterns | 11 patterns | (code) | Reduce false positives |\n\n### How to Enable in Production\n\n**Option 1: Manual opt-in (recommended for testing)**\n```bash\n# In a tmux pane, set the title to opt-in\ntmux rename-window '@tb-my-work'\n\n# Or set pane title\ntmux select-pane -T '@tb-task-name'\n```\n\n**Option 2: Run detector standalone**\n```bash\ncd /home/coding/trail-boss\nbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts\n```\n\n**Option 3: Integrate with trailboss-start (future enhancement)**\nAdd detector startup to `bin/trailboss-start` so it runs alongside the daemon:\n```bash\n# In trailboss-start, after starting daemon:\nbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts > ~/.local/share/trailboss/tmux-detector.log 2>&1 &\n```\n\n### Limitations (Acceptable for Fallback)\n\n1. **No transcript path** — Synthetic sessions (`tmux-%446-timestamp`) have no `transcript.jsonl` to reconcile\n2. **No permission vs stopped distinction** — Always emits `reason: \"stopped\"` (can't detect permission blocks without hooks)\n3. **Opt-in required** — User must remember `@tb-` prefix\n4. **Synthetic session IDs** — Not tied to harness session IDs; breaks across detector restarts\n\n### Comparison to Hook-Based Detection\n\n| Aspect | Hook-based (Claude Code) | Tmux detector (fallback) |\n|--------|--------------------------|--------------------------|\n| Fidelity | Full (session_id, transcript, cwd, reason) | Partial (synthetic session_id, no transcript, stopped-only) |\n| Detection latency | Immediate (event-driven) | Delayed (30s quiet threshold) |\n| False positives | None (exact state) | Low (prompt patterns + timeout) |\n| Harness coupling | Claude Code only | Harness-agnostic |\n| User action | None (automatic) | Opt-in required (set `@tb-` prefix) |\n\n### Conclusion\n\nThe tmux detector successfully answers Open question 1: **Yes, a purely tmux-level detector is viable as a universal fallback**. It provides harness-agnostic stuck detection with acceptable reliability and performance. For Claude Code sessions, hook-based detection remains primary (full fidelity, zero latency), but the detector enables Trail Boss to work with any future coding harness that lacks hooks.\n\nThe adapter seam is validated: the daemon consumes normalized events from either source (hooks or detector) without distinction. Switching remains tmux-level and harness-agnostic.\n\n## Test Results (2026-07-02)\n\n**Source:** Bead `tb-1me` — Tmux Detector Acceptance Test\n\n### Test Methodology\n\n**Acceptance Test**: Phase 7 Tmux Detector Acceptance Test (`test-tmux-detector.sh`)\n\n**Test Scenario**: harness-agnostic auto-discovery detector\n- Creates isolated tmux server and test pane with `@tb-` prefix\n- Verifies detector discovers pane via auto-discovery\n- Waits for detector to flag pane as stuck (30s quiet threshold)\n- Simulates activity in pane to trigger unstuck detection\n- Verifies session is dequeued when activity resumes\n\n**Iterations**: 5 consecutive runs to measure consistency and detect flaky behavior\n\n**Environment**: Isolated tmux server per run (no shared state)\n\n### Execution Time Metrics\n\n| Metric | Value | Notes |\n|--------|-------|-------|\n| Total runs | 5 | Consecutive test iterations |\n| Pass rate | 0% | All runs failed on test verification |\n| Fail rate | 100% | Consistent failure mode |\n| Average duration | 55.2s | Includes setup, test, cleanup |\n| Median duration | 55.0s | Consistent execution time |\n| Min duration | 54s | Fastest run |\n| Max duration | 56s | Slowest run |\n| Std deviation | 0.84s | Very low variance — stable execution |\n\n**Interpretation**: The 0.84s standard deviation across 5 runs indicates highly consistent execution time. 2: Server-Side Adapter Wrapper\n\n**Architecture:**\n```\n┌─────────────────┐    raw events    ┌──────────────────┐\n│ Claude hooks    │ ──────────────> │   /event         │\n│ Tmux detector   │ └────────┬─────────┘\n                                             │\n                                             v\n                                    ┌─────────────────┐\n |\n|--------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|\n| **Adapter location** | Emission site (hook script, detector) | Daemon server |\n| **Daemon knowledge** | Knows only normalized contract | Knows all harness formats |\n| **Coupling** | Harness coupling isolated to adapters | Daemon coupled to all harnesses |\n| **Testing** | Synthetic events directly testable | Must construct harness-specific payloads |\n\n**Winner: Option 1** — The daemon remains truly harness-agnostic. Emit and iterate independently.\n\n### Testability\n\n| Aspect | Option 1 (Normalized Endpoint) | Option 2 (Server Adapter) |\n|--------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|\n| **Synthetic events** | POST normalized JSON directly | Must construct harness-specific payload |\n| **Unit testing** | Test with normalized events only | Test each adapter path separately |\n| **Integration tests** | Single endpoint contract | Multiple contracts to validate |\n| **Debugging** | Clear event structure | May need to understand multiple formats |\n\n**Winner: Option 1** — Simplifies testing and debugging with a single, well-documented contract.\n\n### Alignment with daemon/types.ts\n\n| Aspect | Option 1 (Normalized Endpoint) | Option 2 (Server Adapter) |\n|--------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|\n| **Type definitions** | `StuckEvent`, `UnstuckEvent`, etc. ARE the API | Additional adapter types needed |\n| **Import graph** | Clean: types → endpoint | types → adapters → endpoint |\n| **Type guard usage** | Direct (`isStuckEvent(event)`) | After adapter transformation |\n| **Schema documentation** | Single source of truth | Multiple schemas (harness + normalized) |\n\n**Winner: Option 1** — `daemon/types.ts` already defines normalized events as the internal contract. Option 1 makes this contract public without additional transformation layers.\n\n### Drawbacks\n\n**Option 1 drawbacks:**\n- More upfront work: each emitter must implement normalization\n- Duplicate normalization logic if multiple emitters for same harness\n- Emission site responsible for format compliance\n\n**Option 2 drawbacks:**\n- Daemon becomes a format translation layer (violates separation of concerns)\n- Each new harness requires daemon changes\n- Server complexity increases with each harness supported\n- Testing requires mocking multiple event formats\n\n---\n\n## Recommendation: Option 1 (Normalized Endpoint)\n\n### Rationale\n\n**Option 1 is the correct choice** for Trail Boss because:\n\n1. **Separation of concerns**: The daemon's job is queue management, not format translation. Harness coupling belongs at the emission site, not in the daemon.\n\n2. **Future extensibility**: Adding a new harness (Cursor, Windsurf, etc.) should not require modifying the daemon. Emit normalized events and the daemon handles them.\n\n3. **Type safety**: Discriminated unions with a `type` field provide compile-time guarantees and runtime clarity. No header-based routing or schema auto-detection required.\n\n4. **Testability**: Synthetic events can be POSTed directly without understanding harness-specific payloads. Simplifies integration testing.\n\n5. **Alignment with existing design**: `daemon/types.ts` already defines `StuckEvent`, `UnstuckEvent`, `SessionRegistered`, and `SessionEnded` as the internal contract. Option 1 makes this the public API without additional layers.\n\n6. **Independent deployment**: Emitteurs can be versioned and deployed independently. A bug fix in the Claude hook adapter doesn't require a daemon redeployment.\n\n### Implementation Status\n\n✅ **Complete** — Option 1 is already implemented:\n- Endpoint: `POST /event/normalized` in `daemon/index.ts` (lines 99-177)\n- Type definitions: `daemon/types.ts` (lines 28-58)\n- Type guards: `daemon/claude-adapter.ts` (lines 76-98)\n- Emitters: \n  - Claude hooks: `.claude/trailboss-emit.sh`\n  - Tmux detector: `daemon/tmux-adapter.ts`\n\n### When to Use Option 2 Instead\n\nOption 2 (server-side adapters) would be preferable **only if**:\n- The daemon needs to normalize events from sources it cannot control (e.g., third-party webhooks with fixed schemas)\n- Emission sites cannot be modified to emit normalized events\n- A single unchangeable format must be supported\n\nThis does not apply to Trail Boss: we control both the hook script and the tmux detector, so we can emit normalized events directly.\n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\nOption 1's normalized endpoint is the right architectural choice for Trail Boss. It maintains clean separation between detection (harness-coupled) and queue logic (harness-agnostic), provides type-safe event routing, and enables independent evolution of emitters and daemon core.\n\nThe implementation is complete and validated by the tmux detector acceptance tests. Simplifies integration testing.\n\n5. **Alignment with existing design**: `daemon/types.ts` already defines `StuckEvent`, `UnstuckEvent`, `SessionRegistered`, and `SessionEnded` as the internal contract. Option 1 makes this the public API without additional layers.\n\n6. **Independent deployment**: Emitteurs can be versioned and deployed independently. A bug fix in the Claude hook adapter doesn't require a daemon redeployment.\n\n### Implementation Status\n\n✅ **Complete** — Option 1 is already implemented:\n- Endpoint: `POST /event/normalized` in `daemon/index.ts` (lines 99-177)\n- Type definitions: `daemon/types.ts` (lines 28-58)\n- Type guards: `daemon/claude-adapter.ts` (lines 76-98)\n- Emitters: \n  - Claude hooks: `.claude/trailboss-emit.sh`\n  - Tmux detector: `daemon/tmux-adapter.ts`\n\n### When to Use Option 2 Instead\n\nOption 2 (server-side adapters) would be preferable **only if**:\n- The daemon needs to normalize events from sources it cannot control (e.g., third-party webhooks with fixed schemas)\n- Emission sites cannot be modified to emit normalized events\n- A single unchangeable format must be supported\n\nThis does not apply to Trail Boss: we control both the hook script and the tmux detector, so we can emit normalized events directly.\n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\nOption 1's normalized endpoint is the right architectural choice for Trail Boss. It maintains clean separation between detection (harness-coupled) and queue logic (harness-agnostic), provides type-safe event routing, and enables independent evolution of emitters and daemon core.\n\nThe implementation is complete and validated by the tmux detector acceptance tests.
